existing_interactions.hypothesis: BTTS-no is dominated by 0-0, 1-0 and 0-1 cells so rho changes the price more than lambda for low-scoring pairs.
Hot-keeper form regresses; the shrunk keeper effect, not recent clean sheets, should enter clean-sheet markets.
Missing first-choice defenders matter more for the team that already concedes openly; effect is convex in lambda.

btts_and_clean_sheet.existing_mechanism: BTTS requires each team to score at least once, so it is controlled by the lower-lambda team's probability of scoring and by the dependence between scoring events. Keeper quality, defensive absences and tempo shift clean-sheet probability; the dependence parameter shifts the joint zero-zero and one-nil cells. First-half variant is lower-count and more dependent on the half split.

Tie rules and wording decide equality outcomes.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Posterior strength uncertainty flattens favourites' title probability; fixed-strength sims overstate it.
Deep cup runs reduce league strength more for thin squads, making title and trophy futures negatively linked.
In tight races, head-to-head fixtures and tie-break order determine more of the outcome than average schedule difficulty.

competition_winner_and_top_n.existing_mechanism: Title and top-N prices are outputs of a season simulation: remaining fixtures from calibrated goal models, strength uncertainty and drift, schedule order and tiebreak rules. Multi-competition futures need a joint fixture-list simulation where one team's cup run affects its league strength. Top-N rungs must be consistent with winner and relegation probabilities, and rule wording (playoffs, ties) is decisive.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: High-press teams get a larger first-half share, so period lambdas depend on style, not on a league-average split.
First-half draw probability is the intersection of dependence and low lambdas, so the two must be jointly modelled.
Second-half goal multipliers depend on half-time score and on bench strength after substitutions.

first_half_and_period.existing_mechanism: Half-window markets are the same goal process restricted to 45 minutes plus stoppage. The key parameters are each team's first-half goal share, early-match caution and the distribution of low counts (many 0-0, 1-0). Draws are very likely in first-half result markets, so dependence and draw propensity dominate. Second-half markets need conditional modelling from half-time state and substitution dynamics.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Consistency between hazard integral and the 0-0 cell is a check on the goal model.
High-press sides score earlier so hazards peak early rather than being proportional to full-match lambda.
Dead-ball and penalty events provide step increments in hazard not captured by open-play xG.

first_to_score_event.existing_mechanism: First-to-score is a race between two inhomogeneous Poisson processes with a null outcome for 0-0. The team with higher early hazard (press intensity, set-piece threat, penalty probability) is favoured beyond share of lambda, and the null outcome mass depends on low-score dependence. Rules for own goals and abandoned matches determine settlement.
first_to_score_event.label: First team to score

existing_inputs.label: Opponent- and venue-adjusted xG attack/defence ratings
existing_inputs.why: Lambdas for both teams - the channel through which it moves the Handicap and exact score price.

existing_inputs.label: Dixon-Coles low-score dependence (rho)
existing_inputs.why: Low-score cells dominate exact scores.

existing_inputs.label: Goal-count distributions, correlation
existing_inputs.why: Joint distribution (over-dispersion).

existing_inputs.label: Rating uncertainty and strength drift
existing_inputs.why: Lambda uncertainty fattens margin tails.

existing_inputs.label: Home advantage by team, competition and venue type
existing_inputs.why: Home offset shifts handicap center.

existing_inputs.label: Confirmed XI quality vs season-average XI
existing_inputs.why: Lineup effect on goal difference.

existing_inputs.label: Game state effects, red cards, substitutions
existing_inputs.why: Late-chase dynamics produce larger margins.

existing_inputs.label: Implied goal expectations from handicap and total lines
existing_inputs.why: AH/total implied lambdas calibrate the grid.

existing_inputs.label: Favourite-longshot and draw-price distortions
existing_inputs.why: Long-shot cells are systematically distorted.

existing_inputs.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder
existing_inputs.why: Handicap steps must be monotone.

existing_inputs.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording
existing_inputs.why: Push, half/quarter-line and void rules.

existing_inputs.label: Team xG for/against, shot quality, set-piece xG
existing_inputs.why: Raw team xG for lambda estimation.

existing_inputs.label: Confirmed lineups timestamped
existing_inputs.why: Confirmed XI changes margin expectation.

existing_inputs.label: Set-piece attack vs defence matchup
existing_inputs.why: Dead-ball mismatch moves narrow margins.

existing_inputs.label: Fouls, cards by team/player, referee card tendencies
existing_inputs.why: Red-card risk fattens margin tails.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Integrating lambda uncertainty fattens tails; ignoring it under-prices big margins and high scores.
Fitted rho and lambdas must be consistent with AH and total lines; residual score cells are the exact-score signal.
Late game chasing makes heavy favourites' margin distribution depend on bench depth and substitutions.

handicap_and_exact_score.existing_mechanism: Handicap and exact-score markets are functionals of the full joint goal distribution: handicap prices need the goal-difference distribution including margins, and exact score prices need every cell. They are sensitive to the distribution tail, dependence parameters and lambda errors. Push/split rules for integer and quarter lines matter. The edge, if any, is more likely in consistency across rungs than in a lineup effect.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Lineup shortfalls reduce the attack/defence components separately, so a missing striker mainly lowers own goals and a missing centre-back mainly raises opponent goals.
Dead-rubber matches raise rotation, which changes both expected strength and the draw share.
Evenly matched teams at a strong-HFA venue convert draw mass to home wins; in neutral venues the draw share is higher.
Price comparison needs favourite-longshot and draw-bias correction to avoid false edges on the draw rung.

match_result_3way.existing_mechanism: A joint goal model converts opponent-adjusted attack/defence strengths and home advantage into the 3-way probability vector. The draw is the hard part: it depends on closeness, total expected goals, Dixon-Coles dependence and team draw propensity. Incremental information arrives through confirmed lineups, rotation and stakes, so the price must be updated for team news that is stale in earlier quotes. A two-way winner wording changes how draws are treated (void/advancement/extra time) and must be parsed.
match_result_3way.label: Match result (3-way / two-way winner)

Advancement = 90-minute win + draw x (ET win + shootout); the required-goals state changes each term differently.
A deduction can move a team across the cut and alter tiebreak order, non-additively.

relegation_qualification_advancement.existing_mechanism: These markets are threshold events near the table's cut line, where small rating differences, tiebreak order, points deductions, and motivation (dead rubbers) matter most. Tournament advancement also uses group permutations, tie-break rules, and knockout extra time/penalty components; advancement is not the same as 90-minute result. Slot allocation (cup winners freeing places, coefficient places) changes qualification thresholds.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Tempo scales both teams' lambdas multiplicatively, so high-tempo matchups of two attacking sides produce more extra goals than additive terms predict.
Weather suppresses possession-and-press styles more than direct styles, changing the weather sign by matchup.
Rung residuals vs a fitted distribution identify mispricing independent of team views.
A weaker keeper plus a rotated defence raises opponent scoring convexly.

total_goals.existing_mechanism: Total goals is the sum of two correlated, over-dispersed count processes. Price requires team-pair lambdas (attack x opposing defence, home effect), tempo/openness, lineup quality, set-piece/penalty channels and a count distribution that handles low scores and uncertainty. The ladder of rungs must form a consistent distribution; kinks across rungs indicate pricing noise. Weather, referee and game state add smaller adjustments.

unreg:corners_and_cards_team_events.existing_mechanism: Corners follow territorial pressure, wing play and blocked shots; cards and fouls follow referee tendencies, derby intensity, tackle volume and score state. existing_inputs.label: Player shot/xG/xA rates and minutes
existing_inputs.why: Per-90 xG and xA with minutes shrinkage is the base scoring rate.

existing_inputs.label: Player shot and shot-on-target share of team volume
existing_inputs.why: Share of team shots by role and set-piece duty converts team expected goals into player expected goals.

existing_inputs.label: Confirmed lineups timestamped
existing_inputs.why: Confirmed starters and positions about an hour before kickoff decide whether the player plays and where.

existing_inputs.label: Expected minutes and rotation risk for a player
existing_inputs.why: Expected minutes and substitution risk scale every count.

existing_inputs.label: Designated penalty taker status
existing_inputs.why: Penalty duty adds roughly 0.76 expected goals per penalty awarded, concentrated in one player.

existing_inputs.label: Penalty awarded rate, designated taker, referee tendency
existing_inputs.why: Team and referee penalty-award rates set how often penalty duty matters.

existing_inputs.label: Opponent- and venue-adjusted xG attack/defence ratings
existing_inputs.why: Opponent- and venue-adjusted team xG sets the team's goal expectation.

existing_inputs.label: Opponent shots and chances conceded by zone and position
existing_inputs.why: Opponent's conceded zones match the player's shot zones.

existing_inputs.label: Goalkeeper quality and PSxG-GA
existing_inputs.why: Opposing goalkeeper quality shifts conversion.

existing_inputs.label: Finishing over/under-performance vs xG (regression to mean)
existing_inputs.why: Finishing over-performance regresses, so use xG not goals.

existing_inputs.label: Predicted rotation probability
existing_inputs.why: Predicted rotation changes starter probability before lineups are published.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: A penalty taker's goal probability rises when the referee awards penalties at a high rate.
Formation changes redistribute shot share among forwards and wingers.
A positional move changes which conceded zone the player faces.

unreg:player_goal_assist_props.existing_mechanism: Player scoring is team expected goals times the player's share of chances times minutes, adjusted for penalty duty and opponent defensive weaknesses. Lineup confirmation about an hour before kickoff is the decisive information: the same player's probability changes by multiples if he is dropped or moves position. Over-dispersion and correlation with team goals matter for hat tricks and multi-leg combinations.
unreg:player_goal_assist_props.label: Soccer player goals, assists, hat tricks and score-or-assist

existing_inputs.label: Shots and shots-on-target for/against
existing_inputs.why: Team shots and SOT for and against set the volume to be shared.

existing_inputs.label: Player shot and shot-on-target share of team volume
existing_inputs.why: Player share by role converts team volume to player volume.

existing_inputs.label: Confirmed lineups timestamped
existing_inputs.why: Confirmed lineup fixes who plays and in which role.

existing_inputs.label: Expected minutes and rotation risk for a player
existing_inputs.why: Expected minutes and substitution risk scale every shot and save count.

existing_inputs.label: Expected shots-on-target faced by the goalkeeper
existing_inputs.why: Expected SOT faced is the keeper-saves volume.

existing_inputs.label: Goalkeeper quality and PSxG-GA
existing_inputs.why: Keeper quality (PSxG minus goals allowed) shrunk toward average.

existing_inputs.label: Tempo, pressing intensity, possession style
existing_inputs.why: Pressing and tempo change shot volume.

existing_inputs.label: Game state effects, red cards, substitutions
existing_inputs.why: Trailing teams shoot more; leading teams concede more shots.

existing_inputs.label: Opponent shots and chances conceded by zone and position
existing_inputs.why: Opponent block and zone profile changes shot conversion to SOT.

existing_inputs.label: Formation/tactical system and expected pressing matchup
existing_inputs.why: Formation changes who takes shots.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Shot volume is convex in expected deficit: heavy underdogs concede many shots while taking few, changing both player and keeper counts.
Keeper saves depend on volume times shrunk skill; volume dominates unless skill is extreme.
A teammate's absence raises shot share in a position-specific way.

unreg:player_shots_saves_props.existing_mechanism: Shot counts are team shot volume times the player's share times minutes, shaped by game state (trailing teams shoot more) and the opponent's block and press profile. Goalkeeper saves are the opponent's shots on target times the keeper's save probability, which is noisy and must be shrunk. Both are over-dispersed counts and depend on the confirmed lineup.
unreg:player_shots_saves_props.label: Soccer player shots, shots on target and goalkeeper saves
unreg:player_shots_saves_props.target: A player's shot or shot-on-target count, or a goalkeeper's saves, relative to a threshold.

existing_inputs.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording
existing_inputs.why: Rules wording needed for every series because none was sampled.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: A group stage with more lopsided fixtures raises both total goals and the chance of one match with very many goals, because mismatch fattens the right tail of scoring.
A shared tournament effect shifts every match together, so the variance of tournament goals is larger than the independent sum and tail strikes are underpriced if matches are treated as independent.
The longest shootout is the maximum over a random number of shootouts, so the draw count and the sudden-death chance interact to set the extreme.

unreg:tournament_aggregate_event_props.existing_mechanism: These markets settle on a count or extreme drawn from the 104-match tournament: total goals, the single highest score, how many ties go to penalties, how long the longest shootout lasts, whether the eventual winner ever trails, and whether every team scores. The outcome is generated by a goal-environment level for international football, the mismatch mix of the draw, the knockout structure that creates shootouts, and shared tournament-wide factors that make matches correlated; it is not a single-match total or a player race.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Venue and opponent depend on which third-place groups qualify, so the slot assignment is a joint function across groups and cannot be obtained from marginal group probabilities.
Close group tables resolve on tie-break order, so the probability of a team taking a slot is sensitive to how goal difference and head-to-head are ordered.
A player contract needs the team to arrive, eligibility, and selection; a card ban or rotation can remove a starter even if the team progresses.

unreg:tournament_bracket_composition.existing_mechanism: The occupants and venue of a numbered tournament match come from structure plus results: the schedule fixes the stadium and date of each match number, group finishing positions and the cross-group ranking of third-placed teams map to knockout slots through a fixed table, and each slot is filled by simulated results. A player appears only if his team reaches the match and he is available and selected. The mechanism is bracket plumbing, not the match result or the tournament winner.
